skillSays: Go mobile-first: base styles are the phone layout, min-width media queries enhance upward.
Use container queries (container-type: inline-size) so components respond to their own width, not the viewport.
Make type and spacing fluid with clamp() scales instead of fixed px at each breakpoint.
Reach for intrinsic CSS Grid (repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(X,100%),1fr))) before adding breakpoints.
Use dvh/svh instead of 100vh, logical properties (inline/block), and 44px minimum touch targets.
Check for the usual failures: horizontal overflow, fixed px widths, tiny text, squished aspect ratios.

changes: Defined a clamp() type and space scale as CSS variables, so the headline and gutters scale smoothly with no per-breakpoint font sizes
The schedule card is a size container: slots gain a 'Room 1' chip only when the card itself is wide enough, and feature cards switch from stacked to icon-left when their own column allows
Mobile-first nav collapses behind a 44px hamburger with aria-expanded and expands inline at 64em; hero height uses dvh and logical properties (inline-size, padding-block) throughout
Plan cards use an auto-fit minmax grid that wraps from one to three columns on its own, with no media query for the grid itself
Each plan is a container: when it is wide (single column on a tablet) the feature list goes two-column and the price sits beside the title; price size scales with cqi units
Monthly/yearly toggle buttons are 44px tall and get a mobile-safe layout; prices use nowrap so $103.20 never breaks
Form card is a container, so Full name and Clinic size sit side by side only when the card is 32rem+ wide, whatever the viewport is doing
Inputs are 48px tall at 16px so iOS does not zoom on focus; checkbox row and Show/Hide button meet the 44px touch-target rule
Layout is single-column first, two columns from 64em, with min-block-size in dvh rather than 100vh
